hints: Undo the natural logarithm first by exponentiating both sides.
Take natural logarithms again and divide by $2$ to make $y$ the subject; note that real values require $e^x-1>0$.
walkthrough:
Start with the given equation:
$$\ln(1 + \mathrm{e}^{2y}) = x$$

Subtract $1$ from both sides to isolate the exponential term in $y$:
$$\mathrm{e}^{2y} = \mathrm{e}^x - 1$$

Take the natural logarithm of both sides:
$$2y = \ln(\mathrm{e}^x - 1)$$

Divide by $2$ to express $y$ in terms of $x$:
$$y = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(\mathrm{e}^x - 1)$$
